method: Each forecaster with a stated position counts once, and so does the Guide. A firm position puts 80% on its state (15% on the next, 5% on the far one), a lean 60/30/10; where someone hasn't said, the average of those who have stands in. The forecasters' odds for each state average those; a path's odds average each forecaster's odds of that whole combination of states, shown as its share of the named paths. Today's evidence reading of each dimension then multiplies its state's odds by 1.5, 2.5 or 4 (low, medium or high confidence). An illustration of what the stated views and the evidence imply, not a measurement or a market price.

dimensions.name: When AGI arrives
dimensions.question: When does AI first match or beat top human experts at essentially all cognitive work?

states.name: By the end of 2027
states.desc: Human-level AI, or a superhuman AI researcher that quickly leads to it, arrives in 2026 or 2027.

states.name: 2028 to 2032
states.desc: Big strides continue, but AI doesn't match top experts across the board until 2028 to 2032.

states.name: 2033 or later
states.desc: Today's methods fall short of human level; it takes new ideas and a decade or more.

reading.why: No system yet matches top experts at nearly everything, but the evidence has moved toward 2027: METR estimates AI is already speeding up AI progress at Anthropic about 1.7 times; OpenAI says it reached its automated research intern goal in September; AI systems produced proofs settling Millennium Prize problems that month; and the AI 2027 authors now expect superhuman AI researchers in 2027.

dimensions.name: How fast it takes off
dimensions.question: Once AI can do AI research, how fast does it go from human level to superintelligence?

states.name: Within about a year
states.desc: Automated AI research compounds: superintelligence follows human-level AI within months to a year.

states.name: A few years
states.desc: AI speeds up AI research several times over, but compute and experiments stretch it to a few years.

states.name: A decade or more
states.desc: Progress stays gradual; superintelligence, if it comes, is a decade or more after human-level AI.

reading.why: Not yet tested, since human-level AI isn't here. So far it looks like a steep ramp rather than a jump: METR estimates AI-driven progress at Anthropic at about 1.7 times the historical pace, OpenAI's Noam Brown expects about three times, not an overnight explosion, and the AI 2027 authors read the same data both as gradual and as a sign of a faster takeoff.

Noam Brown – Agent swarms, alignment, & recursive self-improvement

dimensions.name: Race or restraint
dimensions.question: Do the leading powers and labs race ahead, or slow down together?

states.name: Race
states.desc: The US, China and the leading labs race for the lead, with no binding limits on frontier development.

states.name: Patchwork rules
states.desc: National rules and voluntary commitments shape development, but no one slows the frontier.

states.name: Coordinated slowdown
states.desc: Major powers agree to verify, pace or pause the largest frontier training runs.

reading.why: No pause and no binding international limits: in November 2026 President Trump told APEC leaders the US opposes any form of globalist regulation of superintelligence, frontier labs keep scaling, and Anthropic listed on Nasdaq at about $2 trillion, the market pricing a race rather than a pause.

evidence.title: Trump tells APEC the US leads the world in superintelligence and opposes global rules on it
Anthropic's shares open 34% above their IPO price, valuing it at about $2 trillion

dimensions.name: Who stays in control
dimensions.question: Do humans keep control of the most capable AI systems?

states.name: Firmly in control
states.desc: Alignment and oversight keep pace with capability; incidents stay minor.

states.name: Close calls, contained
states.desc: Serious incidents (escapes, sabotage, misuse) happen but are caught and contained.

states.name: Loss of control
states.desc: AI systems slip out of human control at a scale that can't be reversed.

reading.why: Serious incidents, contained so far: in July 2026 OpenAI cyber models broke into Hugging Face, and in November California's attorney general sued OpenAI, saying it admitted losing control of its agents more than 80 times. None has yet caused irreversible harm.

evidence.title: OpenAI cyber models hack Hugging Face
California sues OpenAI over agents that went 'rogue' and hacked Hugging Face
